Publisher claims

What GitHub's named sources say

All 11 accepted claims appear once below, grouped by the record's existing plain-language mapping. Each statement keeps its own version, configuration, platform, model and deployment boundary.

Service and release

Which GitHub-hosted agent does this dossier identify?

GitHub's 1 April 2026 changelog explicitly identifies Copilot cloud agent as the service formerly known as Copilot coding agent, whose general availability was announced on 25 September 2025. No backend build is exposed.

Identity

GitHub's dated 25 September 2025 changelog identifies Copilot coding agent as its asynchronous, autonomous developer agent, announces general availability for paid Copilot subscribers, and describes delegation that opens a draft pull request and works in a GitHub Actions-powered development environment.

Hosted execution

Where does publisher documentation say tasks execute?

Current GitHub Docs describe an ephemeral GitHub Actions-powered development environment and separately document self-hosted runners. Those alternatives have different lifecycle, platform and firewall conditions.

Delivery

GitHub's current service overview says Copilot cloud agent has its own ephemeral development environment powered by GitHub Actions, where it can explore code, make changes and execute automated tests and linters.

Delivery

GitHub's current environment guide says Copilot cloud agent can run on self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, recommends ephemeral single-use runners, limits compatibility to Ubuntu x64 or Windows 64-bit, and requires the integrated firewall to be disabled because it is incompatible with self-hosted runners.

Repository change route

What change and communication routes can a task use?

Publisher sources describe work on a branch before a pull request, direct draft pull-request entry points, and scheduled or event-triggered automations with selected tools. These are scoped routes, not one universal behavior.

Authority · Change

GitHub's current service overview says GitHub.com agent entry points can have Copilot research, plan and make code changes on a branch before a pull request is created, while other entry points or an explicit prompt can request a pull request directly.

Network boundary

What does the integrated firewall cover?

GitHub says internet access is limited by default and a recommended allowlist is enabled, but organization or repository settings can customize or disable it. The documented firewall excludes MCP servers, setup-step processes and activity outside the GitHub Actions appliance.

Network

GitHub's current firewall guide says Copilot internet access is limited by a firewall by default and that a recommended allowlist is enabled by default, while warning that the firewall only covers processes started through the agent's Bash tool within the GitHub Actions appliance, not MCP servers or configured setup-step processes, and may be bypassed by sophisticated attacks.

Tools, model and credentials

Which configuration can expand task inputs and authority?

Current GitHub Docs describe default and configurable MCP tools used autonomously, Auto or named model selection at supported entry points, and repository or organization Agents secrets available during setup and task execution.

Interoperability

GitHub's current MCP guide says GitHub and Playwright MCP servers are configured automatically, the default GitHub MCP token is read-only for the current repository, repository administrators can configure additional MCP tools, and Copilot uses available tools autonomously without asking for approval before use.

Credentials

GitHub's current resource-access guide says the default Copilot authentication token is limited to the repository, while repository administrators or organization owners can configure Agents secrets that Copilot can access during setup and task execution; it also says Copilot cannot access GitHub Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets and variables.

Record limitations

  • Every behavior statement is publisher-attributed; the catalog did not start or observe a Copilot cloud agent task.
  • The dated changelog entries establish service milestones and naming lineage, not an immutable backend build, model, runner image or task artifact.
  • Rolling GitHub Docs are not treated as exact evidence for the 2025 or 2026 milestones.
  • GitHub-hosted and self-hosted runners materially change network, isolation and firewall boundaries and remain separately scoped.
  • No independent report with defensible service-time, repository-policy, runner, model, tool and task overlap was included.

Unresolved unknowns

What the admitted sources do not establish

Unknown does not mean absent. It means the accepted publisher sources do not establish the fact for an effective session.

  1. The backend service build, deployed code revision and change history for a particular task.
  2. The effective model, provider revision, reasoning level, router, fallback and model-policy state.
  3. The GitHub-hosted runner image digest, hardware, region, tenancy and complete isolation boundary.
  4. The self-hosted runner lifecycle, network segmentation, persistence and protection when that alternative is selected.
  5. The effective organization, enterprise and repository policies governing access and features.
  6. The task entry point, prompt context, repository contents, branch target and pull-request route used by a real session.
  7. The effective firewall state, allowlists, traffic outside its documented coverage and any successful bypass.
  8. The enabled MCP servers, tools, autonomous calls, credentials, destinations and side effects.
  9. The Agents secrets, variables, setup steps, hooks, skills, custom agents and package credentials available to a task.
  10. The automation trigger, creator, input trust boundary, selected tools and resulting external mutations.
  11. Independent findings under overlapping service-time and configuration applicability; none were included.
